Reproducibility is the ability of others to repeat a computational or experimental study and obtain the same result, and to build on it. For data-driven and AI-based work it depends on sharing far more than a narrative description: trained parameters, hyperparameters, data and preprocessing steps, code, and for language-model systems the model version and prompts. Related discussions appear in [Agentic AI](/papers/topics/agentic-ai/) and in the summaries [xin2025](/papers/xin2025/) and [kitchin2025b](/papers/kitchin2025b/).

## Reporting machine-learned models (2018)

Kitchin identifies reporting as perhaps the most significant challenge for ML in catalysis ([Kitchin 2018](/papers/kitchin2018/)). ML models can have hundreds of trained parameters plus many hyperparameters, are expressed as programs rather than equations, are fit to datasets of hundreds to tens of thousands of points, and depend on normalization and scaling pipelines. Narrative Methods sections, figures and current supporting information formats are not effective for conveying all of this, so he argues the community must develop and adopt new ways of sharing data and code. Summary: [kitchin2018](/papers/kitchin2018/).

## Trust in self-driving laboratory data (2025)

Canty et al. argue that concerns about whether [self-driving laboratory](/papers/topics/self-driving-laboratories/) data can be trusted must be met by recording not only inputs and outputs but state and environmental metadata (such as temperature and relative humidity), by calibration, benchmarking and control studies built into workflows, and by reporting operational performance, degree of human involvement, resources used, waste and shortcomings ([Canty et al. 2025](/papers/canty2025/)). They note that few SDL technologies currently include repeatability or reproducibility metrics, that no standards or incentives for such studies exist, and recommend releasing code and data at publication and giving SDLs identifiers (analogous to ORCID) for provenance. Summary: [canty2025](/papers/canty2025/).
